[ota-hal] OTA-1765 — TModal, the shell eleven dialogs hand-copied

Tier 0, step 5. Thirty-three modal files, measured before anything was written.
The ones that look like the game's dialogs all draw the same material — a scrim
at `rgba(0,0,0,0.7)` and a card in `#13110f` rimmed `#c9a86a` — and they fall
into two lineages that even NAME their scrim differently:

    FAMILY A  `scrim`     ground #13110f · rim #c9a86a
    FAMILY B  `backdrop`  ground #17150f · rim varies
    neither   no bordered card at all (pickers, forms)

⚠⚠ AND FAMILY A IS `BrandedModal`'S OWN CARD, RE-TYPED BY HAND. Byte for byte:
`width '100%' · maxWidth 380 · #13110f · #c9a86a 1 · radius 4 · padding 14`.
The census is a PREDICATE rather than a number I remember — a file declaring its
own scrim/backdrop AND a card in that ground and rim. It counted ELEVEN before
this pass and counts NINE after, because the two adopters are the two it no
longer matches. The suite runs the same predicate and NAMES the remaining nine,
so a tenth copy shows up as a failing test instead of as another file nobody
notices for a year. Finishing those nine is the modal sweep, a separate pass:
this OTA extracts, it does not sweep.

⚠⚠⚠ STYLES, NOT A `<TModal>` COMPONENT, AND THAT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A
SHORTCUT. arb73 records iPad/iOS presenting a native `<Modal>` INVISIBLY —
rendering nothing while its backdrop still ate touches — which both hid the door
popup AND blocked the EXIT/room buttons under it. `BrandedModal`'s answer is a
per-call-site choice between a native `<Modal>` and an in-tree absolute overlay.
A component owning the container would have to own that choice too, and would be
re-fighting a shipped device bug for the sake of tidiness. What every one of
them agrees on is the MATERIAL, so the material is what the kit exports.
`inlineScrim` stays in `BrandedModal` for the same reason — it is the workaround's
positioning layer, not modal material, and sweeping it in would sweep the device
bug in with it.

⚠ WIDTH IS A PARAMETER, NOT A VARIANT SET. The measured values are 380, 400, 420
and 440 — four numbers with no shared vocabulary behind them, and inventing
`compact/regular/wide` would be naming a decision nobody has made.

⚠⚠⚠ THE SECOND ADOPTION IS NOT FREE, AND THAT IS THE HALF WORTH READING.
`BrandedModal` moves no pixel — the kit's values ARE its values, which is what
makes this an extraction and not a preference. `HookContinueModal` I reported as
differing in ONE number. It differs in TWO: `maxWidth` 420, and its card carries
NO `maxHeight` at all. So taking the shell there ADDS OTA-1614's 85% cap.
  · That addition is the point, not a side effect. This modal taps its own scrim
    to dismiss, and a card that grows past the screen takes that escape with it.
    Its existing guard is a module-load `Dimensions.get('window')` read — a
    number computed once, before rotation, before a split-screen resize — and it
    caps the stage LIST, not the card. Both stay; they cap different things.
  · ⚠⚠ AND THE CAP NEEDS `flexShrink` ON THE SCROLLING CHILD, WHICH IS WHY ONE
    STYLE LINE MOVED WITH IT. RN views do not shrink by default, so a capped card
    whose ScrollView refuses to yield pushes CONTINUE / TRADE NOW / ABANDON out
    of the bottom — of a modal whose only other exit is the scrim behind them.
    That is the exact bug OTA-1614 fixed in `BrandedModal`, and its answer
    (`flexShrink: 1, flexGrow: 0`) is copied here on purpose. Taking the cap
    without it would have shipped a modal you cannot leave. A test asserts the
    line, and asserts the buttons still sit after the scroll.
The usage contract is written into the kit above the export, because it is a
property of the primitive rather than a note about one adopter: a card that caps
its own height needs a child that can give way.

⚠⚠ THE HELPER CEILING WENT 6 → 7, ARGUED RATHER THAN RELAXED. OTA-1759 split the
kit's export budget into components (≤13) and helpers, precisely so the drawer
could not fill with helpers while the component count sat still. So the raise has
to answer the same question the component budget asks: does it arrive BY
INSTRUCTION, and does it replace copies rather than add a choice? `tModalCard`
does both — it is Tier 0's named step 5, and the material it exports was already
hand-copied into nine dialogs. Tier 0 is a finite, named list with ONE primitive
left (TSheet), so the number is not open-ended; a helper not on that list still
has to make its case from scratch.

⚠⚠⚠ AND IT BROKE OTA-1614'S OWN SUITE, WHICH IS THE THIRD TIME IN THIS ROLLOUT A
PIN WRITTEN AS A FILE-LOCAL LITERAL BROKE WHEN THE VALUE IT NAMES MOVED UP A
LEVEL. That suite asserted `maxHeight: '85%'` by reading `BrandedModal.tsx`, and
went red on a pass that STRENGTHENED the cap rather than dropping it. What
OTA-1614 actually claims is "the card this modal draws is capped", and that is
now two facts — the kit caps its card, and this modal uses the kit's card. Both
are asserted, plus `not.toContain('maxHeight')` so a second uncapped copy cannot
reappear locally. The pin follows the CLAIM, not the address.

⚠⚠⚠ AND OTA-1762'S SUITE PINNED THE RATCHET'S CURRENT VALUE, WHICH IS THE SECOND
TIME IN THIS ROLLOUT I HAVE MADE EXACTLY THIS MISTAKE. It asserted
`const BASELINE = 369;` — and OTA-1759's suite did the same thing with 373, from
a pass about ROWS, and I loosened it one OTA later saying so. A ratchet's whole
point is that it MOVES: a suite that pins today's number turns every correct
future removal into a red test, which is the opposite of what a ratchet is for.
What OTA-1762 can honestly claim is that its four declarations went and the
number never climbs back — so it now asserts `≤ 369` and its own ledger line.
The lesson did not stick the first time because I fixed the INSTANCE rather than
the habit; writing it in both suites is the attempt to make it stick.

⚠ FAMILY B AND THE SEMANTIC RIMS ARE NOT SWEPT IN, BY INSTRUCTION.
`MissionComplete` rims in a green and `FusionPicker` in a slate — those are a
SUCCESS and a CATEGORY, not accents, and the owner's amendment reserves semantic
colour. Family B's darker ground is a real second lineage; merging it is a
decision for the sweep, not a side effect of extracting Family A.
⚠⚠ AND THE KIT'S COMMENT SAYING SO ORIGINALLY NAMED THOSE TWO HEXES, WHICH IS
HOW OTA-1757'S GATE CAUGHT IT. That gate asserts the semantic authorities'
colours appear NOWHERE in the kit, and it is right to — a kit that names a
foreign palette in a comment is one careless copy-paste from owning it. So the
prose names them by ROLE now. Note the direction: this rollout has repeatedly had
to teach ITS OWN tests to stop grading comments, and here the correct answer was
the opposite — the older gate was right and my comment was wrong. Whether a
mention in prose is harmless depends on what the rule is about, and this one is
about what the FILE contains.

⚠ THE GOLD RATCHET FELL 369 → 367. Two `borderColor: '#c9a86a'` declarations
became one `T.gold` in the kit. The interface count is 362.
⚠ AND ONE LITERAL IS NOT IDENTICAL, WHICH IS A CASE AND NOT A COLOUR. `T.gold`
is `#C9A86A`; both cards declared `#c9a86a`. RN's colour parser is
case-insensitive so the rendered pixel is the same one — but "byte for byte" was
the claim I made about this card, and it is true of the value, not of the string.
The suite says so out loud rather than leaving it for someone grepping for a
lowercase hex and finding the modal no longer has one.

Tests: __tests__/ota1765TheShellElevenCopied.test.tsx (20 tests) — the kit's
scrim and card proved to carry the shipped values and OTA-1614's cap; width
proved to be a parameter and NOT fixed on the card; the arb73 reasoning proved
still present and no `TModal` component proved to exist; ⚠ `BrandedModal` proved
to use the shell on BOTH presentation paths with its own declarations GONE rather
than shadowed, and `inlineScrim` proved kept and proved absent from the kit;
⚠⚠⚠ `HookContinueModal`'s `flexShrink` proved present with the buttons still
after the scroll, and its own `Dimensions` guard proved kept; ⚠⚠ the census
predicate proved the two adopters no longer match it and NAMED the remaining
nine; and the semantic rims proved untouched.
⚠⚠ THREE OF THE TWENTY RESOLVE THE STYLE RATHER THAN READ THE SOURCE, because
that is the only honest way to claim "zero pixels moved": a helper returning an
array can be assembled correctly and still flatten to something else.
`tModalCard(380)` is flattened and compared to the eight properties
`BrandedModal` used to declare, `tModalCard(420)` is proved to differ in exactly
ONE key, and the scrim is flattened against its five.
⚠ The suite strips comments before grading, and asserts the stripper is still
doing something — sixth time in this rollout, and this file's subject is a hex
and a style name, both of which appear in every paragraph explaining them.
